response.query: Under UK Bribery Act 2010, what does Section 7 cover regarding failure of commercial organisations to prevent bribery?
response.answer:
Under the Bribery Act 2010 (Section 7), Source: UK-01 - Bribery Act 2010
Reference: Section 7
Topic: Failure of commercial organisations to prevent bribery
Requirement: A relevant commercial organisation can commit an offence when an associated person bribes another person intending to obtain or retain business or a business advantage for the organisation.
Notes: Programme-approved for extraction; final legal applicability remains subject to authorised Compliance SME validation. (Chunk ID: UK-01-R004-C01, Source ID: UK-01). Section 8 defines an 'associated person' as a person who performs services for or on behalf of the commercial organisation (Chunk ID: UK-01-R005-C01, Source ID: UK-01).

retrieved_evidence.title: Mitigating circumstances
retrieved_evidence.text:
Source: EU-01 - Directive (EU) 2026/1021 on combatting corruption
Reference: Article 16
Topic: Mitigating circumstances
Requirement: Article 16 identifies certain circumstances that national law can treat as mitigating, including effective internal controls, ethics awareness and compliance programmes for a legal person, and rapid voluntary disclosure plus remedial measures. It is a mitigation framework, not a guarantee of reduced liability or a standalone firm-level duty.
Notes: Official EUR-Lex excerpt from Article 16(c). Article 16 requires Member States to ensure specified circumstances may be treated as mitigating under national law; points (c) and (d) apply only to legal persons. Not a standalone direct ABC Shield duty. Pending SME validation.
